issues.description: Packetization buffer gates on payload type instead of frame type, mis-chunking any non-audio bytes payload.
issues.detail: _write_frame buffers any bytes/bytearray payload when fixed_audio_packet_size is set, slicing non-audio control payloads into PCM-sized chunks. The guard should be isinstance(frame, AudioRawFrame), not isinstance(payload, bytes). As written, any future serializer emitting binary control data is silently corrupted.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size has no validation against sample width/rate; misalignment silently produces broken PCM.
issues.detail: packet_bytes must be a multiple of (sample_width * channels) or the receiver gets misaligned PCM. The code accepts any int with no precondition stated or enforced at setup. A 641-byte value on 16-bit mono tears every packet. Either assert the invariant or document and validate it on StartFrame.

issues.description: Trailing buffer is never flushed on stream end; sub-packet remainder is silently dropped.
issues.detail: _audio_send_buffer retains 0 to packet_bytes-1 bytes after each drain, but there is no pad-and-flush on disconnect, EndFrame, or CancelFrame. The serializer's postcondition that all produced bytes reach the wire is violated. Either flush with silence padding on end-of-stream or document the lossy behavior.

issues.description: Real-time pacing is claimed in the changelog but the code only chunks without gating on wall-clock time.
issues.detail: The while-loop emits all full packets back-to-back via immediate await send; nothing ties emission to _next_send_time or a sleep. Either implement pacing tied to the clock, or rename the feature to fixed-size framing only. The current name oversells the behavior.

issues.description: Packetization concern is misplaced in the generic transport; belongs in the Vonage serializer.
issues.detail: 20ms-at-16kHz framing is a Vonage protocol property, not a generic FastAPI transport concern. The chunk/buffer/send logic should be a small pure chunker function or a composing packetizing serializer wrapper, leaving _write_frame as a thin dispatcher. Extract chunk_pcm(buffer, size) -> (packets, remainder) and unit-test it.

issues.description: DTMF digit parsing accepts two undocumented payload shapes instead of pinning the Vonage spec.
issues.detail: deserialize tries message.get('digit') then message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit') with no spec citation. This encodes uncertainty as behavior and will outlive the protocol drift that motivated it. Cite the documented Vonage shape, parse that, and log-and-drop the other (or remove the fallback once confirmed).

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The Vonage serializer itself is mostly clean, but the fixed-size packetization added to FastAPIWebsocketTransport has multiple correctness and contract problems: it gates on payload type rather than frame type (mis-chunking non-audio bytes), accepts a packet size with no alignment validation against sample width, never flushes the trailing remainder at stream end, and oversells "real-time pacing" the code does not actually implement. Five reviewers also agree the packetization concern is misplaced — it belongs in the serializer or a small extracted chunker, not the generic transport. The DTMF parser hedging across two undocumented shapes is flagged unanimously and should be pinned to the Vonage spec.
